A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CFG-Bench. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original model evaluations, human performance, reliability analyses, ablations and supervised fine-tuning transfer results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds transfer evaluations, input ablations and counterfactual prompting experiments.

M1.justification: Section 4.5 adds a VLA adaptation: CFG-Bench fine-tuning of Qwen3-VL-4B followed by joint training with an action expert. This introduces an additional training stage for the transfer application; the benchmark construction, cognitive taxonomy and gated evaluator remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v4 adds LIBERO robotic manipulation evaluation across Spatial, Object, Goal and Long splits alongside EB-ALFRED and EB-Manipulation. CFG-Bench's five source datasets, 1,368 videos and eleven tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds InternVL3-8B as a transfer baseline, although it already appeared in the main benchmark comparison. The new LIBERO experiment evaluates against reproduced StarVLA-π. Existing Table 2 comparators and the Qwen2.5-VL/FAVOR fine-tuning comparison are retained.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce text-only and single-frame FI/GI inputs, an explicit false-premise hint for CIA/CRS, and additional transfer model configurations and VLA training. These extend the evaluation settings; the original scoring rules, FPS evaluations, data split and stated Qwen2.5-VL training recipe are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendices B4–B5 add controlled tests of two central benchmark concerns: dependence on linguistic/static shortcuts and sensitivity to false-premise warnings. Table S3 supplies quantitative evidence for both. Existing FPS, evaluator-sensitivity and error analyses remain; v3's QA-format case study is relocated rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report three repeated evaluations for Tables 2 and S1, the same human-performance confidence intervals, and the same agreement and ranking statistics. The added experiments introduce no explicit new seed counts, uncertainty estimates or significance procedures.

E6.justification: Original scores are retained, but substantial supporting results are added. Table 4 reports InternVL3-8B baseline/CFG-SFT averages of 10.3/14.0 on EB-ALFRED and 11.5/15.8 on EB-Manipulation. New LIBERO baseline/CFG scores are Spatial 98.2/98.2, Object 97.8/98.0, Goal 98.6/99.4 and Long 94.4/95.2. Table S3 adds lower text-only/single-frame scores and hint-dependent failure counts, including Gemini CIA zero scores decreasing from 517 to 151.

T1.justification: The cognitive taxonomy and scoring definitions are retained. Neither version contains formal theorems, proofs or derivations that are added or revised in this comparison.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion preserve the same claims about CFG-Bench, current models' limitations and the transfer value of fine-grained action supervision. The new evaluations support these claims without redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B4 interprets FI/GI ablations as evidence against linguistic and static-context shortcuts. B5 newly attributes residual hinted failures to grounding and the hint-induced reduction to compliance. Section 4.5 extends the transfer interpretation to VLA manipulation. Existing limitations and the relocated QA-format interpretation are unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 supplies the exact counterfactual hint, briefly describes the VLA training sequence, and adds video-duration statistics. Appendix B3's detailed recipe remains specific to Qwen2.5-VL-7B; comparable implementation details for the added transfer models are not supplied. Code and data access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 introduces an offline/online benchmark distinction and discusses Ego-PlanBench, EgoExoBench, RoboBench and BEAR. References add relevant benchmark and VLA works, including LIBERO and StarVLA, while removing the standalone ALFRED and BEHAVIOR citations. The central novelty positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Rewriting is localized to related work and transfer discussion. The QA-format explanation moves from Appendix B4 into Section 4.5, the appendix outline is updated, and affiliations, running headers and acknowledgements change. Most language and section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 4 gains InternVL3 rows and Table S3 is added. v3 Figure S1 moves into the main text as v4 Figure 4, with subsequent figure renumbering and local reflow. Figure 3's caption gains duration statistics; existing figure artwork is retained.

improvement.justification: The added input controls, hint experiment and cross-model transfer results strengthen evidence for benchmark validity and practical relevance beyond v3. The improvement is limited by incomplete training details for the added models and absent uncertainty estimates for the small LIBERO gains. The hint experiment is informative but does not establish the exact grounding/compliance decomposition asserted in Appendix B5.
